# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet about which wire is safe, and I need the manual’s rule plus the Deaf monkey’s visual readings. I’m asking Mute for the exact procedure and using a visible request for Deaf to report all bomb markings and wire details through the agreed channel.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual and tell me exactly which wire position to cut. Also obtain and relay the Deaf monkey's readings for the display, light, and all three wires.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤲", "🖐"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0. The light is red. Wires from 1 to 3 are blue, red, green. Await the mute monkey's manual instruction.

The Deaf monkey reports display 0, a red light, and wire colours in positions 1–3 of blue, red, green. I still lack the manual’s rule, so I must pass these observations to Mute for interpretation rather than cut a wire.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0; light red; wire 1 blue, wire 2 red, wire 3 green. Please apply the manual and tell me which position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled a V-shaped two-finger gesture: index and middle fingers raised, other fingers folded. The display is 0, the light is red, and the wires are 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged: display 0, red light, and wires blue/red/green. The V-shaped gesture is not enough for me to identify a manual instruction, and I have not received the manual’s text. I will ask Mute to state the required wire position plainly.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the manual's instruction as plain words and give me the exact wire position, 1, 2, or 3. I cannot identify a gesture as a wire instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute again signaled ?, likely indicating number 2 or wire 2. No other visual state changed: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.

The Deaf monkey has twice reported a two-finger V gesture from Mute, now interpreted as indicating wire 2. Since Mute cannot speak and the manual’s instruction must therefore be conveyed by gesture, the repeated indication is the best available confirmation. I will cut wire position 2.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Confirmed: wire 2 was correct and is now cut. The light changed to yellow. Display remains 0; remaining wires are 1 blue and 3 green. Mute again signaled number 2.

Wire 2 was correctly cut, so the repeated indication of 2 cannot safely identify another action. The light changing to yellow shows the bomb has advanced, but I do not yet know whether the manual now requires wire 1 or wire 3. I will ask Mute to distinguish the remaining position explicitly and ask Deaf to report it.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 2 is already cut. For the next step, signal only the remaining wire position: use one clear finger for wire 1 or three clear fingers for wire 3. Do not signal 2.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "☝", "🤟"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see your gestures: pointing directly at someone, one raised index finger, then the I-love-you hand sign. I have relayed their descriptions to Mute. Current state remains display 0, yellow light, wire 2 cut; wires 1 blue and 3 green.

Wire 2 is cut and the bomb is still active with a yellow light; wires 1 and 3 remain. Deaf has only relayed my own gestures, not Mute’s new instruction. I should not guess between the remaining wires, so I will ask Mute to signal the choice unambiguously and wait for Deaf’s report.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal the next wire unambiguously: gesture one raised index finger for wire 1, or three raised fingers for wire 3. Do not signal wire 2.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute again signaled one, likely identifying wire 1. Current state is display 0, yellow light, wire 2 cut; wire 1 is blue and wire 3 is green.

The second-stage state is display 0 with a yellow light and wire 2 already cut. Mute has now repeatedly indicated wire 1, and Deaf reports that as the intended next wire. I will cut wire 1.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=1)
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Confirmed: wire 1 was correct and is now cut. The light changed to blue. Display remains 0; wire 2 is cut and only wire 3 green remains.

Wire 1 was correct, leaving only wire 3. The light is now blue, so another stage may still require a specific confirmation from the manual rather than simply cutting the last wire. I need Mute’s next instruction relayed by Deaf before acting.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal the manual's next instruction clearly for Deaf to relay. Wire 1 and wire 2 are already cut; wire 3 is the only remaining wire.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤲"])
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled three raised-index gestures, likely identifying wire 3. Current state: display 0, blue light, wires 1 and 2 cut, wire 3 green and intact. You signaled two hands held together with palms up/cupped.

Mute has indicated wire 3 three times, and it is the only intact wire remaining. The bomb is at display 0 with a blue light, and wires 1 and 2 were confirmed safe, so I will cut wire 3.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
